pairs.subject: packaging
pairs.evidence: tv-app/build.gradle.kts:23 The release build configuration defines minification settings without configuring code signing credentials, signature verification, or installed-tree acceptance testing for the packaged application.

techniques.evidence: tv-app/build.gradle.kts:23 The release build configuration defines minification settings without configuring signing credentials or an automated post-packaging signature verification gate.

tv-app/build.gradle.kts:43 Testing executes solely as JVM unit tests without an automated clean-environment ladder to install the APK on a target device, verify the installed tree, test launch smoke, and verify removal.
tv-app/build.gradle.kts:14 Specifies minSdk without an enumerated machine-readable OS and architecture matrix, per-cell automated acceptance jobs, or native binary architecture sniffing.
tv-app/build.gradle.kts:66 The debug variant introduces debug tooling dependencies not present in release without an automated drift gate or allowed-divergence specification to ensure variant parity.

tv-app/build.gradle.kts:104 Companion web assets are dynamically injected into the package assets directory without a versioned payload manifest declaring required payloads or verifying presence and absence.

tv-app/build.gradle.kts:12 Application identity is pinned in versioned configuration, but the five installer lifecycle transitions (upgrade, repair, downgrade refusal, uninstall) are unscripted and untested.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard title and introduction frame the subject jurisdiction as desktop applications, but the same lifecycle obligations (signing, installed-tree acceptance, payload verification, OS/architecture matrices) govern client and embedded applications such as Fire TV / Android TV APK packaging; the scope statement should be generalized to client/device application packaging.
